############ I-0526 ############

THE 'instance' ATTRIBUTE IS THE LEAK MECHANISM, NOT THE SORRY -- and de-instancing can make a leak PROBE go vacuously clean.

Two lessons from closing the flat-pullback exactness leak in Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (run 0068, ajc-fbc, commits df899aa50 and 519eecb15). Both generalise to the sibling instHasPicScheme situation and to any future sorry-bodied instance.

LESSON 1 -- DE-INSTANCE IT. A sorry-bodied INSTANCE is qualitatively worse than a sorry-bodied theorem, and the fix is one keyword. As an instance, pullback_preservesFiniteLimits was found by typeclass synthesis anywhere in scope, so a declaration that merely QUANTIFIED over it reported clean axioms while every SYNTHESIS SITE silently acquired sorryAx -- contamination with no textual trace. Changing 'instance' to 'theorem' and citing it with haveI at its (two) real consumers means:
  before: 'theorem q {g} [Flat g] : PreservesFiniteLimits (pullback g) := inferInstance' ELABORATES and reports sorryAx.
  after: the same inferInstance FAILS to synthesise; a consumer must name the theorem, and the dependency appears in the proof term.
Cost: zero (lake build AlgebraicJacobian stayed green at 8762 jobs). Do this the moment you introduce a sorried instance, not later.

LESSON 2 -- THE PROBE THAT MEASURED IT MAY BECOME VACUOUS, AND WILL LOOK LIKE PROGRESS. scripts/axiom-frontier.lean measured the leak with
  leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits (S) : PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 S)) := inferInstance
using the IDENTITY morphism because Flat (𝟙 S) synthesises for free. After de-instancing, that probe went from sorryAx to CLEAN -- not because anything was proved, but because for the identity the pullback IS the identity functor (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId) and synthesis found a different, clean route. A session reading the diff would have seen a leaking line become clean and reported a closure that did not happen.

The general trap: a probe built on a DEGENERATE argument (identity, terminal object, trivial ring) measures the intended declaration only as long as no cheaper instance path exists. Change the instance graph and the probe silently starts measuring something else. Two defences, both now in the file:
 * probe over a GENERAL argument and NAME the carrier rather than synthesising it -- the only honest way to measure a non-instance;

THE 'instance' ATTRIBUTE IS THE LEAK MECHANISM, NOT THE SORRY -- and de-instancing can make a leak PROBE go vacuously clean.

Two lessons from closing the flat-pullback exactness leak in Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge (run 0068, ajc-fbc, commits df899aa50 and 519eecb15). Both generalise to the sibling instHasPicScheme situation and to any future sorry-bodied instance.

LESSON 1 -- DE-INSTANCE IT. A sorry-bodied INSTANCE is qualitatively worse than a sorry-bodied theorem, and the fix is one keyword. As an instance, pullback_preservesFiniteLimits was found by typeclass synthesis anywhere in scope, so a declaration that merely QUANTIFIED over it reported clean axioms while every SYNTHESIS SITE silently acquired sorryAx -- contamination with no textual trace. Changing 'instance' to 'theorem' and citing it with haveI at its (two) real consumers means:
  before: 'theorem q {g} [Flat g] : PreservesFiniteLimits (pullback g) := inferInstance' ELABORATES and reports sorryAx.
  after: the same inferInstance FAILS to synthesise; a consumer must name the theorem, and the dependency appears in the proof term.
Cost: zero (lake build AlgebraicJacobian stayed green at 8762 jobs). Do this the moment you introduce a sorried instance, not later.

LESSON 2 -- THE PROBE THAT MEASURED IT MAY BECOME VACUOUS, AND WILL LOOK LIKE PROGRESS. scripts/axiom-frontier.lean measured the leak with
  leakProbe_pullback_finiteLimits (S) : PreservesFiniteLimits (Scheme.Modules.pullback (𝟙 S)) := inferInstance

After de-instancing, that probe went from sorryAx to CLEAN -- not because anything was proved, but because for the identity the pullback IS the identity functor (Scheme.Modules.pullbackId) and synthesis found a different, clean route. A session reading the diff would have seen a leaking line become clean and reported a closure that did not happen.
